title: Conlon and Rao, "The Cost of Curbing Externalities with Market Power: Alcohol Regulations and Tax Alternatives" (Journal of Political Economy, forthcoming)
paper: Christopher T. Conlon and Nirupama S. Rao, The Cost of Curbing Externalities with Market Power: Alcohol Regulations and Tax Alternatives, Journal of Political Economy, forthcoming
package_label: the authors' repository [chrisconlon/Liquor_Replication_JPE](https://github.com/chrisconlon/Liquor_Replication_JPE), README Entry Point 2 (no NielsenIQ access)
cost_basis: typical on-demand price for a 4 vCPU, 16 GB cloud machine

setup.cmd: python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -q -U pip && venv/bin/pip install --uploaded-prior-to 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z -r requirements.txt

outputs.convert: venv/bin/python -c "import sys, pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet(sys.argv[1]).to_csv(index=False, float_format='%.17g'))" {in}
venv/bin/python -c "import sys, pandas as pd; print(pd.read_parquet(sys.argv[1]).to_csv(index=False, float_format='%.17g'))" {in}

scope_notes: Entry Point 2 of the README: demand estimation from the provided `estimation_data/`, then the counterfactuals and their tables. Stage 1 (cleaning from NielsenIQ) needs licensed data and is not run.

The README's Stage 3 asks for `slow_paper.pickle` from a Dataverse DOI marked TBD. That file is not in the repository, so here it is produced by the README's own Stage 2 command (`estimate_demand_MAIN.py`) and used by every later step.

Not run: the nested logit, demographics-only and fast RCNL specifications (they feed no main-text table compared here), the rho grid, and the five appendix notebooks. Figures 7 and 8 are hashed only. The paper's PDF was not compared.
deviations: Package versions: `pip install --uploaded-prior-to 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z -r requirements.txt`, so pip chooses what was current the day after the package commit (19 Mar 2026). In run 1, plain `pip install -r requirements.txt` resolved pyblp 1.3.0 (Oct 2026), which rejects the package's micro dataset before estimation starts.
`mkdir -p checks` before any step: `1_descriptive_tables.py` saves to `checks/`, which is not in the repository.

Order: the README's stage order (estimation, then Stage 3.1 descriptive tables onward), not the order written in the protocol, so that Table 2 reads this run's marginal costs. The protocol addendum records this.
